title: SPARC Bilateral Phrenic Neurophysiology Preparation with Phrenic Afferent Stimulation
author: Kristi Streeter
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgfyjtpw
materials: Isolate bilateral phrenic nerves using a dorsal approach:

steps.title: Induce and Maintain Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia and transition the animal to a surgical station.

substeps.instruction: Induce with 2.5-3% isoflurane in 100% O2 in a closed chamber for 3-5 minutes.
Transfer to nose cone and maintain at 3% isoflurane in 100% O2.
Place an intravenous line into the tail vein (flush with heparinized saline) for delivery of drugs, anesthesia, and fluids.
Reduce isoflurane to 1% and begin urethane infusion (1.8g/kg in ddH2O at 6ml/hr) while slowly decreasing isoflurane.
Confirm adequate plane of anesthesia via toe pinch and transfer to surgical station.

steps.title: Stabilize Physiological Parameters
steps.instruction: Maintain body temperature and establish mechanical ventilation.

substeps.instruction: Measure body temperature via rectal probe and maintain at 37.0 +/- 0.5 C using a heated surgical table.
Perform tracheostomy and initiate mechanical ventilation: rate = 70 breaths/minute; tidal volume = (0.7 x body weight in grams) mL.
Set inspired gases to 50% O2 + a small percentage of CO2 to maintain target end-tidal CO2 at ~45mmHg, balanced with N2.

steps.title: Perform Initial Surgical Procedures
steps.instruction: Perform vagotomy and establish arterial blood pressure monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Perform bilateral vagotomy.
Make a 1/2 inch ventral incision just distal to the groin on the inner thigh to expose the femoral artery, vein, and nerve.
Gently dissect surrounding fascia to isolate the femoral artery.
Tie off the distal end of the femoral artery and place a loose suture at the proximal end; use an alligator clamp to pull the suture and temporarily prevent blood flow.
Make a small partial incision into the femoral artery wall and insert the arterial catheter ~1 cm into the proximal portion of the vessel, loosening the proximal suture to allow advancement.
Tie the catheter into the vessel using the proximal suture and secure with additional sutures as needed.
Ensure no kinks in the vessel and open the stopcock to ensure unresisted flow.
Flush the catheter with heparinized saline and connect to the pressure transducer/amplifier.

steps.title: Isolate Phrenic Nerves
steps.instruction: Expose and isolate the bilateral phrenic nerves.

substeps.instruction: Using a cautery, perform a ~2 inch incision just lateral to midline and medial to the shoulder blade.
Using a cautery, dissect the dorsal musculature connecting the medial border of the scapulae to the posterior trunk on both sides.
Reflect the medial border of the scapulae and secure with an alligator clip.
Dissect deep thoracic wall muscles and overlying fascia to expose the brachial plexus.
Locate the tendon running horizontal above the brachial plexus, pass 4.0 suture under it twice, place a basket stitch, and pull toward the midline to open the phrenic pocket.
Cut the brachial plexus distally and reflect the nerve bundle to expose the phrenic nerve.
Using fine forceps, isolate the phrenic nerve from surrounding fascia without touching or pulling the nerve.
Section the nerve distally and carefully desheath the proximal end (~1 mm).
Add 0.9% saline to the phrenic pocket.
Repeat the isolation process for the right phrenic nerve.

steps.title: Perform Dorsal Rhizotomy (Optional Group)
steps.instruction: Remove dorsal rootlets for animals in the dorsal rhizotomy group.

substeps.instruction: Using cautery, make a ~1 inch medial incision from the base of the skull.
Cut through underlying muscles to expose vertebral processes; use cautery to separate musculature from C2 and a microcurette to remove muscles from C3-C6 vertebrae.
Using ronguers, remove the left portion of C3-C6 vertebrae.
Using microscissors and fine forceps, cut and remove the dura over C3-C6.
Visualize and cut all dorsal rootlets from C3-C6 with microscissors.
Place saline-soaked cotton above the spinal cord.

steps.title: Set Up Phrenic Nerve Recordings
steps.instruction: Position electrodes and secure the nerve stumps.

substeps.instruction: Place a magnetic base with an L-shaped rod running lengthwise with the rat and above the midline.
Pull and wrap suture around both tendons around the rod.

Fill the phrenic cavity with 0.9% saline and suck the distal end of the proximal nerve stump into the suction electrode, ensuring the desheathed portion forms a tight seal and the nerve tip is visible and submerged in saline.
Place the uninsulated tip of the outer wire against the proximal stump of the nerve (proximal to the electrode tip) and check signal quality.

steps.title: Post-Surgical Stabilization
steps.instruction: Administer paralytics and fluids, then establish baseline stability.

substeps.instruction: Administer fluids (4:1 ratio of Lactated Ringers Solution + Sodium Bicarbonate) at 1.0 ml/hr.
Administer pancuronium bromide (paralytic): 1g in 1cc delivered via tail vein over 3 minutes.
Set baseline CO2 parameters no sooner than 20 minutes after pancuronium delivery.
Draw an initial blood sample to ensure base excess (SBE) is +/- 3.
Hyperinflate the lungs over 2 respiratory cycles by briefly occluding the expiratory line.
Wait at least 20 minutes before starting the experimental protocol; ensure a stable baseline for at least 15 minutes (no trend increases/decreases in nerve activity > 5%).
Take a blood sample during baseline (separated by at least 5 minutes) to establish baseline blood gas values (Criteria: PaO2 > 150 mmHg; SBE +/- 3).
Wait at least 5 minutes after the blood sample before starting the experimental protocol.

steps.title: Establish Stimulus Response Curve
steps.instruction: Calibrate stimulation thresholds and deliver test currents.

substeps.instruction: Set the inspiratory-triggered stimulation threshold by placing a horizontal cursor in the middle of the contralateral integrated phrenic amplitude.
Attach the left phrenic electrode to the stimulator and record from the right phrenic electrode.
Deliver the first current: biphasic, inspiratory-triggered stimulation using a wide pulse (each phase 1.0ms) for 20 seconds.
Turn off stimulation and record output for 5 minutes.
Repeat until all 4 currents have been delivered.
Draw a blood sample after the 4 currents; adjust inspired gas concentrations to keep PaCO2 within 2 mmHg of baseline and PaO2 > 150 mmHg.

steps.title: Experimental Stimulation and Recording
steps.instruction: Deliver prolonged stimulation and monitor blood gases.

substeps.instruction: Deliver inspiratory-triggered stimulation at 90uA for 30 minutes.
Take a blood gas sample 15 minutes after the onset of stimulation.
Continue recording for 60 minutes, taking blood gases at 15, 30, and 60 minutes.
Ensure PaO2 remains above 150 mmHg at all subsequent blood draws.

steps.title: Final Response and Analysis
steps.instruction: Induce hypercapnia and analyze collected data.

substeps.instruction: At the end of the experiment, deliver 12% inspired CO2 to induce hypercapnia for maximum response.

Analyze bilateral phrenic activity (amplitude and frequency), blood pressure (systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressures), and heart rate at baseline, during/after each current, and during hypercapnia.
